演奏蛋形沙鈴時，以手握持蛋形外殼，內部裝有種子或金屬珠等鬆散物。發聲靠搖動使內容: To play an egg shaker you hold the egg-shaped shell in your hand; inside are loose things such as seeds or metal beads. The sound comes from shaking so that the contents strike each other and hit the inside wall of the container. Beginners can start with an up-and-down shake for a faster stream of strokes, then shake side to side to hear the difference. A more advanced move is to grip the shaker in the palm, shake it up and down and open the hand, which produces a swirling sound.

蛋形沙鈴又稱 ganzá，屬手持打擊樂器，發聲分類為體鳴樂器。來源資料指出其為拉: The egg shaker, also called ganzá, is a hand-held percussion instrument, classed by sound production as an idiophone. The source describes it as a Latin American instrument, easy to obtain because it is cheap and relatively simple to play. Its development is tied mainly to Latin American percussion traditions, and it can be used alongside instruments such as the bell shaker; it also appears in samba groups and mariachi bands. The source gives no specific years, names or further history of its spread, so more historical detail cannot be added.
蛋形沙鈴常見於拉丁美洲音樂場合，常與馬拉卡斯等手搖打擊樂器搭配使用，也出現在森巴: The egg shaker is common in Latin American music, usually alongside hand-shaken percussion such as the maracas, and it also appears in samba groups and mariachi bands. A mariachi line-up may include drum kit, piano, saxophone, bass, violin, vihuela, guitarrón and trumpet, with an acoustic or electric guitar and voices added occasionally.
蛋形沙鈴的琴身通常以塑膠模製成，外形呈卵形，由兩半組合成容器；發聲體為裝入其中的: The body of an egg shaker is usually moulded from plastic in an oval shape, two halves joined into a container; the sounding part is the metal beads or seeds inside, which strike each other and the inner wall when shaken. The source also notes that seeds and plastic are cheap materials. As for the other parts — the closure, the surface coating or the fittings — the source says nothing.
蛋形沙鈴的聲音來自容器內種子或珠子相互碰撞，並撞擊內壁所產生的短促打擊聲。上下搖: The egg shaker's sound comes from the seeds or beads inside the container striking each other and hitting the inner wall, a short percussive sound. Shaking up and down gives a faster stream of strokes, and shaking side to side gives a slightly different timbre; gripped in the palm and shaken while the hand opens, it gives a swirling sound that other percussion finds hard to make. The principle is close to the shaker — both are shaken idiophones — but the shell is oval or egg-shaped. The source gives no range.
蛋形沙鈴（ganzá）是手持體鳴樂器，外殼卵形，內裝種子或珠子，搖動時互相撞擊發: The egg shaker (ganzá) is a hand-held idiophone with an oval shell holding seeds or beads that strike each other when it is shaken. It can be shaken up and down or side to side, or gripped in the palm and released to make a swirling sound. It comes from Latin America, is cheap and easy to play, is often used with the shaker and appears in samba groups and mariachi bands, alongside drum kit, piano, saxophone, bass, violin, vihuela, guitarrón, trumpet, acoustic guitar, electric guitar or voices.
